title: Bibha Chowdhuri: The Beam of Light that Lit the Path for Women in Indian Science

topics.title: Bibha Chowdhuri: the physicist who studied cosmic rays

learn.hook: Somewhere in the night sky, there is a star named after an Indian woman scientist. Who was she?
points: The lesson tells the life story of Bibha Chowdhuri, an Indian physicist whose work lit the way for women in Indian science.
Bibha Chowdhuri was born in 1913 in Calcutta (now Kolkata). She studied physics at the University of Calcutta at a time when very few women studied science.

At the Bose Institute in Kolkata, she worked with the physicist D. M. Bose. They used photographic plates to detect tiny particles produced by cosmic rays, which are high-energy particles that reach the Earth from outer space.

She earned her PhD at the University of Manchester in England, working in the laboratory of Patrick Blackett, who won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1948. Back in India she worked at research centres such as the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and the Physical Research Laboratory.
In 2019, the International Astronomical Union named a star 'Bibha' in her honour.

example.q: Read this original passage: 'In the 1930s, most girls in Bengal were not encouraged to study science. Bibha chose physics anyway, sat in classrooms full of young men, and went on to study particles that come from far beyond the Earth.' Think it through: which two qualities does this passage show?
steps: Girls were not encouraged, yet she chose physics: that shows courage and determination.
She went on to study particles from space: that shows curiosity and love of science.
The word 'anyway' shows that she did not let others' expectations stop her.
example.answer: Determination (she chose physics anyway) and curiosity (she studied particles from beyond the Earth).

learn.reallife: When you see a girl topping a science olympiad or building a robot at a school fair, she is walking on a path that pioneers like Bibha Chowdhuri helped to open.

quiz.q: Bibha Chowdhuri was a scientist in which field?
quiz.explain: She was a physicist who studied particles produced by cosmic rays.

options: High-energy particles that reach the Earth from outer space

quiz.mistake: Thinks 'rays' must mean ordinary light

quiz.q: In which city was Bibha Chowdhuri born?
quiz.explain: She was born in Calcutta, now called Kolkata.
quiz.mistake: Picks another big Indian city

quiz.q: With which scientist did she work at the Bose Institute?
quiz.explain: She worked with D. M. Bose at the Bose Institute in Kolkata.

quiz.q: In which year was a star named 'Bibha' in her honour?

quiz.q: Read: 'Bibha chose physics anyway, sat in classrooms full of young men...' What does 'anyway' show?
options: She went ahead even though girls were not encouraged
She was forced to study physics

quiz.q: Where did Bibha Chowdhuri earn her PhD?

teach.nudge: What kind of scientist was she? What did she study? And what was named after her?

topics.title: Women in Indian science: pioneers and the words to describe them

learn.hook: A botanist who improved sugarcane, a 'weather woman', a 'missile woman' and an astronaut! India's women scientists have done it all.
points: Janaki Ammal was a botanist who worked on breeding better sugarcane. Asima Chatterjee was a chemist who studied medicines made from plants.
Anna Mani was a physicist and meteorologist who made instruments for measuring the weather. Kamala Sohonie was a biochemist who studied the nutrition in foods.

Kalpana Chawla, born in Karnal, Haryana, became the first woman of Indian origin to go to space, in 1997. Tessy Thomas, a scientist at DRDO, is known as the 'Missile Woman of India' for her work on the Agni missiles.
A pioneer is one of the first people to do something and so opens the way for others. Many of these women were pioneers.
Words to describe them: determined, brilliant, dedicated, inspiring, persistent. Nouns: determination, dedication, inspiration, achievement.

example.q: Think it through: Read: 'India had to buy most weather instruments from abroad, so Anna Mani helped design and build them in India.' Choose the best adjective for her: lazy, resourceful or careless.
steps: India lacked its own weather instruments.
Instead of depending on others, she helped make them in India.
A person who finds clever ways to solve problems is resourceful.

learn.reallife: Today women scientists lead missions at ISRO, research medicines in labs and teach science in colleges across India, building on these pioneers.

quiz.q: Who is known as the 'Missile Woman of India'?
quiz.explain: Tessy Thomas of DRDO worked on the Agni missiles.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the scientists and their fields

quiz.q: Janaki Ammal was a ___.
quiz.explain: She was a botanist, a scientist who studies plants, and she worked on breeding better sugarcane.
quiz.mistake: Does not link Janaki Ammal with plants

quiz.q: What is a pioneer?
options: One of the first people to do something, opening the way for others
A person who gives up easily
quiz.explain: A pioneer goes first and makes it easier for others to follow.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'pioneer'

quiz.q: Anna Mani is best remembered for work on ___.
quiz.explain: Anna Mani designed instruments to measure the weather.
quiz.mistake: Confuses her with other scientists

quiz.q: Choose the noun form: 'Her ___ to science inspired many students.'
quiz.explain: After 'Her' we need a noun: dedication.
quiz.mistake: Uses the adjective or verb where a noun is needed

quiz.q: Read: 'India had to buy most weather instruments from abroad, so Anna Mani helped design and build them in India.' Which word best describes her?
quiz.explain: She found a practical way to solve the problem, which is what a resourceful person does.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the action in the sentence to judge the character

quiz.q: Kalpana Chawla was born in which state?
quiz.explain: Kalpana Chawla was born in Karnal, Haryana.

teach.nudge: What does a pioneer do first? And how does that help the people who come after?

topics.title: Writing about a life: relative pronouns

learn.hook: 'Bibha was a physicist. She studied cosmic rays.' Two short sentences, or one smooth one? Relative pronouns do the joining!
points: A relative pronoun joins two ideas and refers back to a noun: who, which, whose, whom, that. 'Where' and 'when' can join clauses about places and times.
who = for people: Bibha was a physicist who studied cosmic rays.
which = for things and animals: The star which was named after her is far beyond our Solar System. That can be used for people or things in many sentences.
whose = shows possession: D. M. Bose was the scientist whose laboratory she worked in.
where = for places; when = for times: Kolkata is the city where she was born. 1913 was the year when she was born.

example.q: Think it through: Join these sentences with a relative pronoun: 'Kalpana Chawla was an astronaut. Her first space flight was in 1997.'
steps: The second sentence talks about something that belongs to Kalpana Chawla: 'her first space flight'.
example.answer: Kalpana Chawla was an astronaut whose first space flight was in 1997.

learn.reallife: Biographies, encyclopedias and school project reports use relative pronouns to pack facts smoothly: 'Kolkata, where she was born, ...'

items.text: Anna Mani was a scientist ___ built weather instruments.
This is the telescope ___ my school bought.
She is the girl ___ project won first prize.
Ahmedabad is the city ___ the Physical Research Laboratory is located.
I remember the day ___ Chandrayaan-3 landed.

quiz.q: Join with a relative pronoun: 'Bibha was a physicist. She studied cosmic rays.'
options: Bibha was a physicist which studied cosmic rays.
Bibha was a physicist who studied cosmic rays.
Bibha was a physicist whose studied cosmic rays.
Bibha was a physicist where studied cosmic rays.
quiz.explain: 'Who' is used for people.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'which' for a person

quiz.q: Which relative pronoun shows possession?
quiz.explain: 'Whose' shows that something belongs to someone: the girl whose bag is red.
quiz.mistake: Confuses 'whose' with 'who's' (who is)

quiz.q: Choose the correct option: 'This is the microscope ___ we used in the lab.'
quiz.explain: A microscope is a thing, so use 'which' (or 'that').
quiz.mistake: Uses 'who' for a thing

quiz.q: Choose the correct option: 'Kolkata is the city ___ Bibha Chowdhuri was born.'
quiz.explain: 'Where' introduces a clause about a place: the city where she was born.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'which' without a preposition for a place

quiz.q: Join: 'I met a scientist. Her book is about stars.'
options: I met a scientist who book is about stars.
I met a scientist whose book is about stars.
I met a scientist which book is about stars.
I met a scientist where book is about stars.
quiz.explain: 'Her book' shows possession, so 'whose' replaces 'her'.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'who' where possession must be shown

quiz.q: Choose the correct option: 'The bus ___ goes to Ooty leaves at six.'
quiz.explain: A bus is a thing, so we use 'which' (or 'that').
quiz.mistake: Uses 'who' for a thing

quiz.q: Choose the correct option: '1997 was the year ___ Kalpana Chawla first flew to space.'
quiz.explain: 'When' introduces a clause about a time.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'where' for a time

quiz.q: In 'The girl who won the quiz loves physics', the relative pronoun is ___.
quiz.explain: 'Who' joins the clause 'who won the quiz' to 'the girl'.
quiz.mistake: Picks the noun instead of the joining word

teach.ask: Gappu wrote: 'Anna Mani was a scientist. She made weather instruments.' How can he join these into one sentence?
teach.praise: Perfect! 'Anna Mani was a scientist who made weather instruments.' 'Who' is a relative pronoun used for people!
teach.nudge: Which joining word do we use for a person? Can it replace 'She'?
